artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n):M^{2n}\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be an algebraically integrable Hamiltonian system on a real symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, with $n\le 3$. Here "integrable" means that $f_1,\dots,f_n$ are Poisson-commuting functionally independent functions, and "algebraically integrable" means that the system extends to a complex algebraic completely integrable system, i.e. the generic complex fibers are open subsets of abelian varieties and $f_1,\dots,f_n$ are polynomial (or algebraic) in suitable coordinates.

A singular point of $F$ is a point $p\in M$ where $df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_n$ vanishes. Two singular points (or their germs/saturated neighborhoods) are called topologically equivalent if there exists a homeomorphism of neighborhoods sending leaves of the singular Lagrangian foliation defined by $F$ to leaves, and symplectically equivalent if there is a symplectomorphism realizing this equivalence.

Problem:
(a) Describe (classify) all topological types of singular points and singular fibers of $F$ that may occur in algebraically integrable systems with $n\in\{1,2,3\}$ degrees of freedom, locally and semi-locally (in a saturated neighborhood of the singular fiber).
(b) For each topological type appearing in (a), determine a complete set of symplectic invariants classifying such singularities up to symplectic equivalence.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of topological and symplectic types of singularities in (algebraically) integrable systems with up to three degrees of freedom remains an active research area. Partial results exist: nondegenerate singularities are well understood in two degrees of freedom (Eliasson, Vũ Ngọc, Zung), and recent work (e.g., 2023 arXiv preprint on saddle-focus singularities) gives semi-local topological classifications for specific singularity types in three degrees of freedom. Symplectic invariants have been obtained for certain unfoldings of $A_n$-singularities. A general classification covering all topological types and symplectic invariants in the algebraically integrable case for $n\le 3$ is not available, and the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Classification of saddle-focus singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm for topological classification of nondegenerate saddle-focus singularities of integrable Hamiltonian systems with three degrees of freedom up to semi-local equivalence.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (partial) progress on semi-local topological classification of a specific singularity type in three degrees of freedom.

status_evidence.title: Symplectic Classification for Universal Unfoldings of $A_n$ Singularities in Integrable Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Real-analytic symplectic normal forms for integrable Hamiltonian systems near singular points of type universal unfolding of $A_n$, with semilocal and semiglobal classifications.
status_evidence.claim: Symplectic invariants are known only for restricted classes of singularities, not the full classification asked for.

status_evidence.title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists describing topological types and symplectic invariants of singularities of algebraically integrable systems with $\le 3$ degrees of freedom as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is recorded as open in a problem list on finite-dimensional integrable systems.
